title: Made in His image
teaser: You did not earn your dignity. You were given it on the sixth day, before you ever did a thing.
framework: Genesis 1:26-31 — Human dignity is grounded in God who made us, not in achievement, status, or output.

panels.heading: BEFORE YOU DID ANYTHING
panels.content:
Yesterday we sat with the start of everything. Today we meet ourselves inside that start.

God has made stars and oceans and birds. He has named light and dark. And then, on the sixth day, He pauses.

He does not pause to make a better fish. He pauses to make you.

Before you ever earned a paycheck, before anyone praised you, before anyone wrote you off, God spoke a word over your kind. He said it was good. He said it was very good.

Your worth was settled before your résumé existed. Settle in. This is where Genesis is taking us.

panels.heading: THE WORD GOD USED
panels.content:
Read the passage slowly:

*"Then God said, 'Let Us make man in Our image, after Our likeness, to rule over the fish of the sea and the birds of the air, over the livestock, and over all the earth itself and every creature that crawls upon it.' So God created man in His own image; in the image of God He created him; male and female He created them. God blessed them and said, 'Be fruitful and multiply, and fill the earth and subdue it...' God looked upon all that He had made, and indeed, it was very good. And there was evening, and there was morning—the sixth day."* (Genesis 1:26-31, BSB, abridged)

The Hebrew word for image is **צֶלֶם** (*tselem*). In the ancient Near East, a *tselem* was usually a statue. Kings would set up images of themselves at the edges of their territory to declare, *I rule here, even when I am not standing here.* That is the word Moses chooses for us.

What the surrounding cultures did with stone, the God of Israel does with people. Every human being is a living statue at the edge of His kingdom, declaring His rule, bearing His likeness, reflecting His face into the world.

Notice also the strange plural: *Let Us make.* Christians have long heard the Trinity humming under that line. It is not a knockdown proof. It is more like an early echo of what John 1 will sing out loud: God was never alone, and the One who made you was already a fellowship of love.

panels.heading: THE DIGNITY YOU CANNOT EARN OR LOSE
panels.content:
If image is the foundation, then everything modern life hands you about identity is upside down.

You were not made worthy by what you produce. You were made worthy by Whose likeness you carry. Calvin, in his Institutes, put it bluntly: the imago Dei extends to the whole person, so that there is no part of us, however broken, in which some sparks do not glow. He wrote that even when staring down at human cruelty in his own century. The image is defaced in us, but it is not erased.

This is the doctrine that quietly underwrites everything Scripture will later say about the unborn, the enslaved, the foreigner, the dying, the difficult neighbor, and the enemy across the line. They are tselem too. So is the person you scrolled past with contempt this morning.

And this is the dignity Christ comes to restore. Paul calls Him "the image of the invisible God" (Colossians 1:15). The blurred picture of God in us is brought back into focus by the perfect picture of God among us. "Just as we have borne the image of the earthly man, so also shall we bear the image of the heavenly Man" (1 Corinthians 15:49).

panels.heading: WHAT THIS ASKS OF YOU TODAY
panels.content:
Image-bearing is not a feeling. It is a fact you live inside.

It means the tired person across from you at breakfast is a walking statue of God. So is the coworker who annoys you. So is the political opponent you find hardest to listen to. So is the version of yourself you are quickest to despise.

N. T. Wright argues that the human vocation in Genesis 1 is priestly: we exist to reflect God's wise care into creation, and to gather creation's praise back to Him. That is your job description, before any other job description.

So today, try this. When you meet someone you would rather diminish, pause for one second and remember the word tselem. Do not perform kindness. Just stop dismissing them in your head. Let the image you both carry become visible again.

panels.heading: A PRAYER
panels.content:
Father,

You made me on purpose, in Your image, before I had done anything good or bad.

Give me eyes today to see Your face in the people I am tempted to write off: the loud one, the difficult one, the one whose politics I cannot stand, the one I pretend not to notice.

Reshape me into the likeness of Christ, who is Your true image.

Amen.
